public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 769

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos769

open Filter

open scoped Topology

/-- An axis-parallel homothetic copy of the standard `n`-cube. -/
structure Cube (n : ℕ) where
  lower : Fin n → ℝ
  side : ℝ

/-- Membership in the half-open cube `∏ j, [lower j, lower j + side)`. -/
def Cube.Mem {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, Q.lower j ≤ x j ∧ x j < Q.lower j + Q.side

/-- Membership in the half-open unit cube `[0,1)^n`. -/
def InUnit {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 ≤ x j ∧ x j < 1

/-- A cube is nondegenerate and contained in the closed unit cube. -/
def Cube.InsideUnit {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) : Prop :=
  0 < Q.side ∧ ∀ j, 0 ≤ Q.lower j ∧ Q.lower j + Q.side ≤ 1

/-- `tiles` is an exact decomposition of the unit `n`-cube into `k` homothetic
cubes: every tile is a positive homothet inside the unit cube, and every point
of `[0,1)^n` belongs to exactly one half-open tile. -/
def IsTiling {n k : ℕ} (tiles : Fin k → Cube n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (tiles i).InsideUnit) ∧ ∀ x, InUnit x → ∃! i, (tiles i).Mem x

/-- Exactly `k` homothetic `n`-cubes can tile the unit `n`-cube. -/
def Admissible (n k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ tiles : Fin k → Cube n, IsTiling tiles

/-- `c` is the minimal cutoff `c(n)`: every `k ≥ c` is admissible, and (when
`c > 0`) `c - 1` is not. -/
def IsCutoff (n c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k, c ≤ k → Admissible n k) ∧ (c = 0 ∨ ¬Admissible n (c - 1))

/-- The highlighted conjecture `c(n) ≫ n^n`: there is an absolute positive
constant `A/B` with `c(n) ≥ (A/B) n^n` for all sufficiently large `n`. -/
def Erdos769LowerBound : Prop :=
  ∃ A B N : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧
    ∀ n c : ℕ, N ≤ n → IsCutoff n c → A * n ^ n ≤ B * c

/--
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

The `c(n) \gg n^n` conjecture is **false**: for odd `n`, one can tile the unit
`n`-cube into `k` homothetic cubes for every `k ≥ U(n)` with `U(n)/n^n → 0`, so
`c(n)/n^n → 0` along odd dimensions and no absolute constant lower-bounds it.

Determining good bounds for `c(n)` in general remains open.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-769/Research/Solution.lean"]
theorem erdos_769 : answer(False) ↔ Erdos769LowerBound := by
  sorry

/--
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.
The cutoff condition is restricted to positive dimensions: in dimension zero,
exact coverage permits only one tile, so no cutoff exists.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_769.variants.growth_rate :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧
        ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos769

findings.description: The Boolean question in lines 97–99 asks whether log(c(n))/(n log n) converges to some unspecified real γ. This is an additional regularity question, not an equivalent formulation of the source's request to give good bounds for c(n): quantitative bounds need not entail convergence of this normalized logarithm, and answering the convergence question need not determine an asymptotic bound or even γ. The docstring explicitly introduces this interpretation, so it is a defensible but debatable research variant rather than a demonstrated falsehood.
findings.source_evidence: https://erdosproblems.com/latex/769 asks: “Give good bounds for c(n) — in particular, is it true that c(n) ≫ n^n?” Erdős, “Remarks on some problems in number theory” (1974), §II, pp. 199–200, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf, discusses improving bounds and specifically conjectures c(n)>n^n when n+1 is prime. Neither source poses the logarithmic-limit question.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm and document this as an independently proposed additional question, rather than an equivalent replacement for the remaining bounds problem. To formalize the latter directly, ask for an unknown bounding/asymptotic function with appropriate quantitative conditions; alternatively, use the explicit prime-dimension conjecture in the cited source.

reformulations.difference: Uses exact, unique coverage by half-open cubes instead of a decomposition into closed cubes with pairwise disjoint interiors.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite family of positive axis-parallel cubes, taking closures of a half-open partition covers the closed unit cube and preserves disjoint interiors. Conversely, perturb a point of [0,1)^n slightly in every positive coordinate direction, choosing the perturbation smaller than its positive distances to the finitely many tile faces. Closed coverage then provides a half-open tile containing the original point. Two half-open tiles containing that point would have overlapping interiors after a sufficiently small positive perturbation. Thus the admissible tile counts are unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Expresses minimality by eventual admissibility together with inadmissibility of c−1, rather than using an explicit least-element operator.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved IsCutoff n c ↔ IsLeast {d : ℕ | ∀ k, d ≤ k → Admissible n k} c. Failure at c−1 rules out every smaller threshold; conversely, admissibility at c−1 would extend the admissible tail and contradict leastness. The c=0 branch handles natural subtraction correctly.

reformulations.difference: Encodes the positive constant in c(n) ≫ n^n using positive naturals A,B and the cross-multiplied inequality A*n^n ≤ B*c.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Proved equivalence to the same eventual inequality with an arbitrary positive real constant δ. In one direction take δ=A/B. In the other choose a positive reciprocal 1/(b+1)<δ and weaken the lower bound. Cross-multiplication is valid because the denominator is positive.

review.notes: All declarations and relevant boundary cases were checked. Scratch proofs establish that no zero-tile tiling exists, one tile always works, Admissible 0 k iff k=1, no zero-dimensional cutoff exists, and a unique cutoff exists in every positive dimension. The growth-rate statement's existential cutoff function cannot artificially force convergence; this was also proved. The cited disproof and all its dependencies were recompiled against the actual reviewed definitions: #print axioms Erdos769.erdos769_lower_bound_false reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. The source still labels the overall bounds problem OPEN, but that alone does not invalidate the solved category on the narrower, verified lower-bound disproof. Experiments and detailed notes are under /workspace/review; the reviewed file was not modified.
